newsitem.title: USA: Calif. quake agency scraps earthquake risk bonds.
newsitem.headline: Calif. quake agency scraps earthquake risk bonds.

text.p: The California Earthquake Authority's governing board on Friday scrapped plans to issue up to $1.5 billion of earthquake risk bonds, according to the authority's interim chief executive officer.
Instead, the authority has entered into a reinsurance contract with the firm of Berkshire Hathaway Inc. for up to the entire $1.5 billion, interim CEO Greg Butler said.
Despite the change in financing, Butler told Reuters the authority was still scheduled to start selling earthquake insurance policies on December 1.

"The board was faced with a decision between the unknown and the known," Butler said. "The fear was that the capital markets pricing was going to be more than we had expected. The board acted to take the known versus the unknown."
As a result of Friday's decision, the earthquake authority expects to buy from $2.4 billion to $3.5 billion of reinsurance, Butler said.
Butler said the authority would consider issuing similar types of bonds in the future. "The capital markets are in the future for the CEA," Butler said.
The California Earthquake Authority's governing board on Friday also extended the deadline for insurance companies to commit themselves to participating in the agency.

The new deadline is November 25, Butler said. Previously, the companies had been expected to submit their contracts by Nov. 15. Insurance companies representing at least 70 percent of the California residential insurance market must agree to participate in the earthquake authority by the new deadline for it to become operational, he said.
"I'm fairly confident we'll have the 70 percent," Butler said.
